title: Time Tag
headline: Dashing around obstacles and rewinding movement.
premise: A tag game with obstacle-aware dashes, movement rewind, round rewards, and saved cosmetic collections.
proof: Movement abilities backed by rewards, shops, and saved progress.

play.title: Dash to a target or rewind your movement
play.description: The game plans a route for the seeker’s dash. Rewind follows a recorded movement sequence, with a ghost and connecting line showing the previous positions. Gameplay videos will be added here.

explode.title: How a dash route is planned and checked
explode.description: The solver checks the level for places the character can stand, then searches walk and jump connections. The movement plays on the player’s computer, with a final position check on the server.

layers.title: 01 / Find possible standing positions
layers.detail: Sample the level and check space above the character.

layers.title: 02 / Choose a route
layers.detail: Search walk, jump, and higher-cost super-jump connections.

layers.title: 03 / Play and check the movement
layers.detail: Run the movement locally, then check its endpoint on the server.

cases.title: Finding a route through the level
cases.player: The game checks obstacles and landing space when planning a dash.
cases.technical: ParkourSolver samples downward hits along a corridor and filters for walkable normals. A five-point upward ray fan checks headroom without treating the empty space above a wedge as an obstruction. Walk edges use passage sweeps. Natural jumps solve vertical projectile motion and test the required horizontal speed, then sweep along the arc. The A* search yields when its configured time budget is used.
cases.tradeoff: Super-jump edges carry an inflated search cost to favor natural routes, so this is not a claim of minimum real travel time. The search uses a linear open list. The arena itself is authored, not procedurally generated.

cases.title: Checking where a dash or rewind ends
cases.player: The player’s computer plays the movement, then the server checks the final position.
cases.technical: Both abilities follow request → server approval → local playback → completion-position report → endpoint validation/reconciliation. Rewind is checked against independent server history; dash uses geometric bounds and landing-clearance checks. Observers receive server-derived replica state with frame-rate-independent smoothing.
cases.tradeoff: The server checks the endpoint, not every movement step. This is neither rollback netcode nor conventional input-replay prediction. Current rewind and solver behavior still need recorded runtime evidence.

cases.title: Saved profiles and prototype trade handling
cases.player: Currency and inventory use a shared saved profile; the prototype also contains trade coordination.
cases.technical: SessionLock stores ownership in the protected DataStore record and uses UpdateAsync to reject an active competing owner, with stale takeover rules. A trade takes two profile/resource types for each of two players in deterministic order, revalidates and snapshots state, then applies the swap with failure and rollback branches.
cases.tradeoff: This is source-inspected prototype architecture, not evidence of a released trading feature or universal fault tolerance. The companion-profile dependency should be rechecked before promoting trading as product scope.

notes: The source audit verifies movement abilities, profile persistence, currency-spend trail crates, and reward/purchase handling. Current gameplay recordings are pending.
No claim of fully server-driven movement, rollback netcode, or a frame-time guarantee is made.

features.title: Dash and rewind
features.description: Dash around obstacles to a target, or retrace earlier movement with a visible ghost and trail.

features.title: Round rewards and leaderboards
features.description: Round results rank players and award coins, keys, and XP.

features.title: Shops and monetization
features.description: The prototype includes currency purchases, purchase-receipt handling, and a rotating trail-crate shop.
features.note: Purchase handling is reviewed in source; current checkout and grants need testing. Subscription IDs still reference the previous game in the audit.

features.title: Cosmetic inventory and saved progress
features.description: Collect and equip trails, with currency, inventory, and progress stored in a player profile.
features.note: The save-and-return clip will show a specific confirmed result, not a guarantee against every save failure.
